preamble: The velar nasal [ŋ] is replaced by the glottal fricative [h] in the Huastecan branch of Mayan: Proto-Mayan *ŋ appears as h in Huastec word-finally, so that Proto-Mayan *q'iiŋ 'sun, day' corresponds to Huastec k'ih, *ʔooŋ 'avocado' to ʔuh, and *laajuuŋ 'ten' to laajuh. The change removes both nasality and oral place of articulation. Other Mayan branches have x (K'iche'an–Mamean) or n (Q'anjob'alan, Cholan, Yucatecan). Parkatêjê and Krikatí (Timbira, Northern Jê) changed the velar nasal to h before nasal vowels, as in kahə̃ 'snake' against Canela kaŋə̃.

examples.note: Kaufman lists Western Huastec k'ij 'tiempo, estación' under Proto-Mayan *q'iinh; Yucatec k'iin and Ch'ol k'in keep the nasal as n.
Compare Yucatec lajun-, Tzotzil lajuneb'; Chuj lajunhe7 keeps the velar nasal.
Only the plain nasal (before nasal vowels) is affected; the postoralized allophone became nk (*ŋgo 'wet' > (-n)ko). Krikatí shares the change.

sources: Kaufman, T. (2003). A Preliminary Mayan Etymological Dictionary. FAMSI. https://www.famsi.org/reports/01051/pmed.pdf
Norcliffe, E. (2003). The Reconstruction of Proto-Huastecan. MA thesis, University of Canterbury. https://glottolog.org/resource/reference/id/109784
Nikulin, A. (2020). Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo. https://repositorio.unb.br/handle/10482/38893
